units.title: React, Vite, JSX, components, props, and lists
units.intro: In Week 8 we built CourseHub by hand: we wrote the HTML, styled it, and then kept the page in step with our data by finding elements, building strings of markup, and replacing what was on the screen every time something changed. This week you will build the same kind of page with React. You will describe what the page should look like for the data you have, and React will update the DOM for you. You will see how a Vite project is put together, write JSX, split a page into components that receive props, and render lists of data with stable keys, then load that data from a real API. Each topic runs in the browser, so you can edit the code, run it, watch the inspector draw your components, and check your work as you go.
localNotes: The Vite scaffold and build steps run on your own computer: you create the project with npm and run npm run build in your own terminal, and the lab shows the exact commands and the output to expect.

units.title: State, events, and component communication
units.intro: In Week 10 we built the product page: a list of cards rendered from data, split into components that receive props. It could show data but not respond to it, because nothing on the page could change. This week the page comes alive. You will handle a click with an event handler, give a component a value it owns with useState, and watch React re-render only the component whose state changed. Then you will meet the problem every real app runs into, two components that need the same value, and solve it the way React does: move the state up to the parent, pass the value down as a prop, and pass a function down so that a child can ask for a change. In Session 1 we draw that sequence on the board as event, callback prop, setter, and re-render; in these topics the inspector's flow view draws it for you from the clicks you make, so you can check your mental model against what React really did.
localNotes: Everything this week runs in the browser. If you want to keep working on your own computer, download a step's workspace and run it with npm install and npm run dev, as you did in Vite project anatomy.
